MedicalJobsAustralia.com     HammondCare Waratah is currently looking for a Weekend Cook-Chef to join our team.

HammondCare has a unique model of care which places the resident's needs as our number one priority.

As a part of the Support Service's Team, you will support our model of care by delivering high quality meals within the MAIN KITCHEN at our Waratah Facility catering for our 232 residents in accordance with the organisational mission and mission in action statement.

Core Responsibilities:

Reporting to the Support Services Manager you will be responsible for;

Preparing nourishing, appetising, and culturally appropriate meals that meet individual dietary needs and preferences. This includes ensuring meals are visually appealing and served at the correct portion size and temperature.

Ensuring strict adherence to the Food Safety Program (FSP), HACCP standards, and all relevant health and safety regulations. This also involves complying with the Aged Care Quality Standards, specifically Standard 6: Food and nutrition.

Preparing residents' specific dietary requirements, including texture-modified food for those with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia).

Responding to feedback and addressing concerns promptly.

Maintaining accurate documentation related to food safety, resident dietary needs, and operational data.

To be successful in this role, you will:

Be flexible and able to commit to a range of shifts including weekends.

Value teamwork but also be able to work independently and show initiative.

Must have experience in cooking for large numbers in a commercial kitchen and or an aged care environment.

Have an understanding of The vulnerable persons guidelines for food safety or willingness to learn and incorporate these into your everyday work routine.

Demonstrated understanding of safe manual handling practices.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Experience in preparing and cooking bulk meals.

What are the benefits of working with HammondCare?

Flexible working environment to deliver a healthy work-life balance.

Gain access to multiple health and fitness facilities at a low fee with Fitness Passport

Be supported & empowered in your role to really make a difference to our residents.

A workplace trainer on each site committed to your ongoing training & development.

Access to not-for-profit salary sacrificing arrangements.

Shift times.

0630-1500

0900-1730

About HammondCare:

HammondCare is an independent Christian charity that has been serving families in Australia since 1932. We are an organisation that is led by our values, our passion is improving the quality of care for people in need.

As one of Australia's most innovative health & aged care providers, we champion life for every person in our care.

Does this sound like you? Apply Now!

For more information, please contact Sarah Egan - segan@hammond.com.au

HammondCare is committed to creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity and inclusion. We strive on creating an equal employment environment where everyone from any background can be themselves.

All short-listed applicants for these positions will be asked to consent to a criminal record check, pre-employment medical assessment & complete a NDIS Worker's Screening check.

Our Talent Acquisition team & Hiring Managers kindly request no unsolicited resumes from recruitment agencies. HammondCare isn't responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.    Click here to Apply now →

 We are seeking a proactive and customer-focused  Human Resources Business Partner (ASO4)  to join a busy SA Government workforce team. This is an excellent opportunity for an HR professional with government experience who enjoys partnering with managers, providing practical HR advice, and supporting a range of workforce activities. Based within a collaborative and high-performing environment, you will play a key role in delivering operational HR services that support organisational objectives. 
 About the Role 
 Reporting to the  Principal Human Resources Business Partner , you will provide human resources advisory and administrative support to business leaders and teams across the organisation. You will work closely with managers to deliver effective workforce solutions while ensuring compliance with government policies, procedures, and employment frameworks.  
 Key Responsibilities 
 
 Provide timely and practical HR advice to managers and stakeholders on a range of workforce matters. 
 Support recruitment, selection, onboarding, and workforce administration activities. 
 Assist with classification and reclassification processes. 
 Prepare HR correspondence, documentation, reports, and workforce-related communications. 
 Maintain accurate HR records and support workforce data management and reporting. 
 Build and maintain effective working relationships with managers and key stakeholders. 
 Contribute to workforce projects, process improvements, and continuous improvement initiatives. 
 Support the delivery of quality customer-focused HR services across the business.  
 
 About You 
 To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate: 
 
 Previous HR experience within the South Australian Government or broader public sector. 
 Experience providing HR advisory support across a range of workforce matters. 
 Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills. 
 Sound understanding of contemporary HR practices and employment frameworks. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
 Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities. 
 A professional, confidential, and customer-focused approach. 
 Experience using HR information systems and workforce reporting tools will be highly regarded.  
 
 Desirable Experience 
 
 HR experience within SA Health, a Local Health Network, or another government agency. 
 Exposure to CHRIS21 or other HRIS platforms. 
 Relevant tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Business, or a related discipline.

HOBAN Recruitment has partnered with a leader in the NDIS Support Disability space.      Working for an organisation that offers compassionate and personalised care to individuals with diverse needs and our dedicated teams provide a range of support services, including NDIS Support Coordination, Psychosocial Recovery Coaching and Allied Health. We strive to empower individuals to lead fulfilling lives and promote inclusivity and accessibility in the community.     The Role       As a  Support Coordinator  you will join the  Campbelltown  team on a permanent full-time basis. The purpose of this role is to work under the Senior Support Coordinator in the company to assist NDIS participants in the coordination of their supports funded in the NDIS plans. The goal is to ensure that participants can achieve their expected goals including of independence and well-being so that they are better able to participate in community.     Main responsibilities include:    
 
 Doing admin work to Coordinate the day-to-day operation of the NDIS Support Coordination Services 
 Contribute towards participant assessment care planning, response to referrals and reviews in line with MDSS'S Policies and procedures. 
 In collaboration develop and promote a team-based approach to deliver participant centered care and services 
 Collaborate with participants, fostering an understanding of their needs and aspirations to explore options and develop actions that best meets their care needs. 
 Gathering data, booking appointments, supports and services 
 
    What you need    
 
 Minimum 6 months to 1 year experience as a Disability Support Coordinator or similar role in disability - knowing the basics. 
 Qualification or enrolled in a course for Disability Services, Aged Care or other relevant Community Services 
 Experience working with NDIS participants with knowledge of NDIS Operational Guidelines 
 Highly developed communication and interpersonal skills 
 Team player who is driven by compassion and role purpose 
 An Australian driver's license, Working with Children Check, National Police Clearance, First Aid Certificate and a NDIS Workers Screening Check 
 Own vehicle and comprehensive car insurance 
 Excellent admin, office and PC skills. 
 Passion to grow to become a Support Coordinator 
 Care Coordinators encouraged to apply 
 
      Benefits    
 
 Flexible start and finish times 
 Lunch provided once a week 
 Access fleet vehicles 
 Parking and expenses paid 
 Monthly employee activities 
 True career progression, take your career where you want it to go!!
